replacements.reviewNotes: The published mainstem has 69/81 Natural Earth Suez Canal matches; nearest candidate Ismailiya Canal has 14/81, and the authoritative Egyptian canal name is Suez Canal, not a river. Public-domain NE supplies geometric identity; government authority supplies the independent waterway name. Only this Hydro system is in scope; the other Suez-labelled logical system has 4/81 NE matches and remains unapproved.

officialNationalAtlasBranchReview.reason: The 2025 National Atlas of Korea (NGII) explicitly distinguishes the Namhangang and Bukhangang geographic branches, which converge at Yangsu-ri to form the downstream Hangang. The independent public-domain Natural Earth polyline named Namhan overlaps 65 of the published Hydro mainstem's 81 samples (0.802), while the downstream Han candidate also overlaps 30/81 (0.370). These are geographic reach names, not competing tributary names or legal stream-register classifications. Retain the existing conventional branch label rather than mislabel the entire river as a distinct statutory watercourse.

replacements.reviewNotes: 65/81 NE Namhan reference matches support the branch label. Official NGII atlas names it a geographic branch, not an administratively separate national river. The original 남한강 label is retained; only OSM metadata, aliases, and independent attribution are corrected.
